$comment: Events seeded into the world that NO fixture names. The world is PERMITTED to be larger than the corpus -- scenario-binding-unbacked asserts fixture-ids SUBSET-OF world and deliberately not the converse -- and the seed-first coordination rule depends on that asymmetry. But an intermediate state that is green is indistinguishable from a transition that never completes, so the orphan set is declared EXACTLY rather than merely permitted. Observed set must EQUAL permanent + every transition's eventIds. An undeclared orphan fails; a declared orphan that does not exist fails just as hard, so an expectation cannot be nudged to match reality.
limitation: Covers event identifiers (evt_*) only. Other entity classes can still be seeded without any fixture naming them, and nothing here reports it.

permanent.why: BEHAVIOURAL scenario. The fixture is a Problem body -- the resident is not authorised for this event -- so it names no event, while the world must contain one for the authorisation check to have something to refuse. Permanent by design, not a stalled transition.

BEHAVIOURAL scenario. The fixture is a Problem body -- the event was retracted -- so it names no event, while the world must contain the retracted one for there to be anything to retract. Permanent by design, not a stalled transition.
